source.title: Spec: carlab.rs polish around two touchpoints, parts-sourcing case studies, incremental builds and cross-site debts

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

source.body:
## Problem Statement

carlab.rs now has its own parts catalogue (PR #357), but the site around it was built before the catalogue existed and has gathered loose ends:

- A visitor comes for one of two things: to book the car service, or to find a part. The homepage and the site structure do not put both paths in front of them with equal weight, and neither path is tuned to end in a contact.
- The visual language drifts: inputs are slightly rounded while buttons are full pills, icons sit on some submit buttons and not on others (#37).
- CarLab now sources parts for customers, but there is no way to show a successful parts-sourcing job as a case study: "parts sourcing" is not a CarLab service, and a case study (Work) cannot name the parts it used.
- Several small defects and debts are open across the three sites: "My garage" remembers VINs the shop could not resolve (#430), wrong price and Serbian on live approved.rs and CarLab case studies (#279), em dashes and Ё in source copy (#278), trust boundaries still without zod (#38), `llms.txt` never audited and no agent catalogue (#285), no social links (#39), the Offer cart and checkout logic spread across routes (#388, #389, #390).
- Every carlab.rs build re-renders every page even when one Part changed, and the real Vercel build of the catalogue was never measured (#380, #40).
- The local-SEO keyword method was only applied to carlab.rs (#268).

## Solution

One pass that leaves carlab.rs coherent and the three sites tidy:

- carlab.rs is restructured around two first touchpoints with equal weight, service booking and part search, each ending in a contact, and a part search leads naturally to booking its installation. The current visual style stays and is polished into consistent rules (one radius scale, one button style, icons only where a button navigates).
- Parts sourcing (the existing VIN parts inquiry) becomes a CarLab service with its own page. A Parts sourcing case study is drafted from a completed shop Order with one button in the shop admin, lists the Parts that Order sourced, and shows its total; Work pages link to those Part pages and Part pages show the Works that used them.
- A shop Order becomes completed when staff mark its Lead won in the CRM bot; ❌ lost in the bot and a cancel in the shop admin cancel each other (ADR-0053).
- A Part that cannot be bought at once shows «Заказать», which opens a Parts inquiry with the owner's wording; every Part shows its supplier photos, or its Category's picture when the supplier has none.
- The listed defects and debts are fixed.
- carlab.rs builds incrementally: a page whose data did not change is not re-rendered; the first real Vercel build is measured.
- approved.rs and details.rs get the corrected keyword research and copy review.

Tickets folded into this spec: #430, #380, #279, #388, #389, #390, #289 (rescoped: polish, not a redesign), #37, #278, #268, #285, #39, #38, #40, plus the new parts-sourcing case studies. Each item below is marked [feature] or [bug].

## User Stories

Site structure and design (#289, #37) [feature]

1. As a driver who needs a repair, I want to see on the first screen of carlab.rs that I can book the service, so that I do not have to hunt for it.
2. As a driver looking for a part, I want the search box on the first screen and in the header of every page (a field on desktop, an icon on phones), so that I can type a VIN, a part number, a name or my car right away.
3. As a visitor on a phone, I want both paths visible without scrolling past marketing copy, so that I reach what I came for in one tap.
4. As a service visitor, I want each service page to show what the service includes, how long it takes and how to book, so that I can decide and book on the spot.
5. As a parts visitor who found a part, I want to see its price or «Заказать», each with a clear next step, so that I know how to get it.
6. As a parts visitor, I want to book the installation of the part I found in the same flow, so that I get the part fitted without a second enquiry.
7. As any visitor, I want the contact options (form, Telegram, WhatsApp, Viber, phone on touch devices) at the end of every path, so that leaving a contact is always one step away.
8. As the owner, I want every path to end in a contact, so that no visit leaves without a way to follow up.
9. As a visitor, I want inputs, buttons and cards to share one radius scale and one button style, so that the site looks deliberate.
10. As a visitor, I want arrow icons only on buttons that take me somewhere, not on buttons that submit a form, so that buttons say what they do (#37).
11. As the owner, I want the design kept in its current style and only polished, so that the brand stays recognisable.
12. As a details.rs visitor, I want the same button rule on details.rs, so that the sister site follows it too (#37 covers both).

Parts sourcing and case studies [feature]

13. As the owner, I want Parts sourcing («Подбор запчастей», today's VIN parts inquiry) to be a CarLab service with its own service page, so that it is sold like the other services.
14. As staff, I want a «Сделать кейс» button on a completed Order in the shop admin, so that a case study starts from a real deal.
15. As staff, I want the button to create an unpublished draft Work in Keystatic with the Order's car (make, model, year), its Parts (brand and number, several of them) and its total in RSD already filled in, so that I only write the story and add photos.
16. As staff, I want the draft committed with my own Keystatic login, so that the shop server never holds a key that can change the repository.
17. As a customer, I want my VIN, name and contact never to reach a case study, so that my deal can be shown without exposing me.
18. As staff, I want the draft's data copied once and editable in Keystatic afterwards, so that the case does not change when the shop does.
19. As staff, I want the button only on completed Orders, so that a case study is always a deal that happened.
20. As a visitor reading a Parts sourcing case, I want each listed Part to link to its Part page when it has one, and to show its brand and number otherwise, so that I can order the same Parts.
21. As a visitor on a Part page, I want to see the case studies where we sourced that Part, so that I trust we have done it before.
22. As a visitor, I want the case to show the price the customer paid, so that I can judge what sourcing costs.
23. As a visitor reading a Parts sourcing case, I want its enquiry form to be about Parts sourcing, so that my enquiry reaches the right person.
24. As the owner, I want Parts sourcing cases translated to sr and en like every Work, and the service in `llms.txt`, the sitemap and the service list, so that every locale, search engine and agent finds them.

Completed orders [feature]

25. As staff, I want marking an Order's Lead ✅ won in the CRM bot to complete the Order in the shop, so that I mark a deal in one place.
26. As staff, I want ❌ lost in the bot to cancel the Order, and cancelling the Order in the shop admin to mark its Lead lost, so that the two never show different outcomes.
27. As staff, I want a status change that could not reach the other side to be retried, so that the bot and the shop end up in step.

Part cards [feature]

28. As a visitor looking at a Part that cannot be bought at once (no Offer yet, or the shop still in closed beta), I want a «Заказать» button instead of «Цена по запросу» or «Узнать цену», so that I can act on it.
29. As that visitor, I want «Заказать» to tell me plainly that the shop is new, works directly with the best suppliers to get good prices, that this number is most likely available but needs checking, and that they will buy it or offer an equivalent once I leave a contact, so that I know what happens next.
30. As a visitor on any Part page, I want «Установить у нас», with the installation price shown where it is set, so that I can have the Part fitted.
31. As a visitor, I want every Part to show a picture: the supplier's photos where they exist, otherwise the Category's picture marked as an illustration, so that no Part looks empty and no Part shows a wrong photo.

Small defects [bug]

32. As a visitor whose VIN the shop could not resolve, I want "My garage" not to remember that VIN, so that the site does not show me a car it cannot match (#430).
33. As a visitor whose VIN resolved, I want "My garage" to keep remembering it, so that I do not retype it.
34. As an approved.rs visitor, I want the bmw-x1-2 case to show 47,000 EUR everywhere, so that the price is consistent (#279).
35. As a Serbian reader, I want the four wrong Serbian phrases in the approved.rs and CarLab cases fixed, so that the text reads correctly (#279).

Copy hygiene (#278) [feature]

36. As the owner, I want no em dash and no Ё in the Russian source copy of the three sites, so that the copy does not read as machine-written.
37. As the owner, I want a check that fails when an em dash or Ё is added to Russian source copy, so that it does not come back.
38. As a content editor using the content skill, I want the rules written into the skill, so that new copy follows them.

Agents and search (#285, #268) [feature]

39. As an AI agent, I want each site's `llms.txt` to follow the format (title, summary, grouped links, a bounded size), so that I can read the site efficiently.
40. As an AI agent, I want carlab.rs's catalogue entries in `llms.txt` to fit the budget, or the overflow to be a recorded choice, so that the file stays usable as the catalogue grows.
41. As an AI agent, I want `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json` on all three sites, so that I can discover what each site offers.
42. As the owner, I want approved.rs and details.rs keyword research done with the corrected method, so that their meta copy targets what people search for.

Social links (#39) [feature]

43. As a visitor, I want to find each brand's social accounts somewhere more visible than the footer, so that I can follow the brand.
44. As the owner, I want the account links to be configuration per brand, so that I can add them when I send them.
45. As the owner, I want a social link not to count as a contact click, so that contact analytics stay clean.

Trust boundaries (#38) [feature]

46. As the owner, I want every remaining trust boundary listed in #38 validated with zod, so that bad input fails loudly instead of slipping through a cast.

Shop internals (#388, #389, #390) [feature]

47. As a developer, I want one reader for Offer cart and order lines, so that line metadata is typed once.
48. As a developer, I want the Offer cart operations behind one module, so that each store cart route is validation plus one call.
49. As a developer, I want checkout to go through one entry point and a pure judge, so that every refusal is decided in one place and unit-tested.
50. As a shopper, I want the cart and checkout to behave exactly as today, so that the refactor changes nothing I see.

Builds (#40, #380) [feature]

51. As the owner, I want carlab.rs to skip re-rendering pages whose data did not change, so that a Publish after a small catalogue change builds fast.
52. As the owner, I want a layout or config change to still rebuild everything, so that incremental builds never serve stale markup.
53. As the owner, I want the first real Vercel production build of the catalogue measured (time, output size), so that we know the margin to the limits.
54. As the owner, I want approved.rs and details.rs build times measured before deciding on incremental builds there, so that we adopt it only where it pays.

## Implementation Decisions

Structure and design (#289, #37)

- The homepage, header and service/part flows are reworked around two equal entry points: service booking and the one search box (`<catalogue-search>`, #428). On phones the search comes first with the services and «Записаться» right under it, both on the first screen. The header carries the search as a field on desktop and as an icon on phones on every page. Both paths end in the existing contact controls and lead form; no new contact mechanism.
- A Part page offers booking its installation where the Part has an installation price, reusing the existing installation data and the lead form with the service the installation maps to.
- The visual polish stays inside carlab.rs's own design system: one radius scale and one button style defined as the app's tokens (never in `packages/site-kit`, per AGENTS.md); which radius and whether buttons stay pills is the designer's call within the current style, as is the arrow rule for buttons (#37, also on details.rs) and where the social links sit (#39).
- Design goes through the `ui-designer` agent and the `frontend-design` skill, mobile first; the parked six-direction redesign is not resumed.

Parts sourcing case studies

- Parts sourcing is the existing `vin-parts-inquiry` service (Glossary: Parts sourcing), promoted into `SERVICE_SLUGS_BY_BRAND.carlab` with its label in `@podbor/brands`, so it gets a service page, appears in the Keystatic multiselect and can be a Work's `servicesApplied`. `parts-order` stays the Lead service of shop Orders.
- The Work schema gains optional sourced Parts (Brand name and part number, normalised with the catalogue contract) and an optional price in RSD shown only on Parts sourcing works; the Keystatic form gets matching fields; neither is translated.
- A completed Order's card in the shop admin gets «Сделать кейс». It opens a page on carlab.rs beside Keystatic (the approved.rs case-photo pattern) that fetches a privacy-filtered summary of that Order from the shop (car as make, model and year; Brand-numbers; total in RSD; never VIN, name or contact) and commits an unpublished draft Work with the staff member's Keystatic GitHub login. The shop holds no repository write token. The draft is a one-time copy; the site build never reads the Order.
- At build time each listed Part resolves against the catalogue snapshot: a Part with a page renders as a link through `PathBuilder`, anything else as brand and number text. Part pages list the Works that reference their Brand-numbers. A missing shop or catalogue never breaks a Work page.
- A Parts sourcing Work's closing lead form posts the Parts sourcing service.

Completed orders (ADR-0053)

- Marking a `parts-order` Lead won in the CRM bot completes its shop Order (picked up and paid); there is no completion from the shop side.
- Lost in the bot cancels the Order; cancelling the Order in the shop admin marks its Lead lost.
- The bot reaches the shop through an authenticated admin route and the shop reaches the bot through the Lead route it already uses; a failed call is retried so the two converge. Glossary: Completed order.

Part cards and images

- Wherever a Part cannot be bought at once (no Offer, or `SHOP_OPEN` unset), the price block shows «Заказать», opening the Parts inquiry form with the owner's copy (new shop, direct work with the best suppliers, availability checked, this Part bought or an equivalent offered, leave a contact). Russian source copy only; the translate job fills sr and en.
- Every Part page offers «Установить у нас», showing the installation price where the Part has one.
- A Part with no supplier photo shows its Category's picture marked as an illustration; supplier photos stay first wherever they exist.

Defects

- #430: the rule "remember only a VIN the shop resolved" lives in one place, inside the site-kit "My garage" element or the code that knows the VIN resolved; site-kit stays at 100% coverage and any site using the element gets the rule.
- #279: price set to 47,000 EUR in the case's structured price and in the FAQ; the four Serbian fixes are hand translations committed on their own, never with a Russian edit (AGENTS.md).

Copy (#278)

- Em dashes and Ё are removed from the Russian source copy of all three sites with the content skill; `translations` blocks and structured fields are not hand-edited (the translate job refreshes them).
- The content skill gains the em-dash and no-Ё rules.
- A check in the `check` job fails on an em dash or Ё in Russian source copy (i18n YAML and Work/case Russian fields), alongside the existing YAML validity check.

Agents and SEO (#285, #268)

- `llms.txt` of all three sites is audited against the format; carlab.rs's catalogue entries fit the budget or the overflow is written down as a choice.
- `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json` is served on all three sites through one shared helper next to the shared `llms.txt` renderer, each site supplying its data.
- WebMCP is not part of this spec (#431).
- #268 is an owner task: it needs live Keyword Planner and Search Console access. The agent side is writing up the research per site and applying the agreed meta copy once the owner supplies the data.

Social links (#39)

- Account URLs are per-brand configuration; placement is decided in the design polish (more visible than the footer); social links never carry the contact-click attribute.

Trust boundaries (#38)

- Every open item in #38's register gets a zod schema at the boundary; schemas for browser code sit beside the browser module, not inside it, so zod does not enter the client bundle (AGENTS.md).

Shop internals (#388, #389, #390)

- One line reader types Offer cart and order line metadata (offer id, parent offer id, add-on kind, in stock, lead time) and the handoff state; add-ons link to their Part by the parent's Offer id; one readiness schema replaces the two copies; beta orders carrying both parent keys still render.
- The Offer cart becomes one module; each store cart route is request validation plus one call.
- Checkout has one entry point and a pure judge returning a refusal code or repriced lines; Medusa sits behind an adapter and Medusa's own completion route uses the same judge.
- These no longer wait for the shop to open: they change no behaviour.

Builds (#40, #380)

- carlab.rs turns on Astro's `experimental.incrementalBuild` (Astro 7.2). Every catalogue page (Part, Model, Vehicle, Model x Category, Category, make hubs) returns a `cacheKey` from `getStaticPaths` that is a digest of exactly the data the page renders, so an unchanged page is skipped and a changed one re-rendered. Astro already invalidates everything on a config, lockfile or module-graph change.
- `build.concurrency` stays at 1 (the cache is off above 1).
- CI persists Astro's cache directory between carlab.rs builds (an Actions cache keyed per branch), since `vercel build` runs on a fresh runner; an empty cache renders everything.
- The decision is recorded in an ADR, including how a stale cache is avoided.
- approved.rs and details.rs: CI build times are measured; incremental builds are adopted there only if the measurement shows a gain worth the `cacheKey` plumbing, and the decision is recorded in #40.
- #380: the first real Vercel production build of the catalogue is measured after the shop's first deploy and the result posted on #380.

## Testing Decisions

A good test drives the feature through its public interface and asserts what a caller sees: page data, element behaviour in the DOM, HTTP responses, stored rows and Leads, committed files. Never internal calls. Seven seams, all existing patterns:

1. Storefront page data through the catalogue snapshot, paths, sitemap and `llms.txt` tests: Works linking to Part pages and plain text for Parts without one, Part pages listing their Works, the Parts sourcing service in `llms.txt`/sitemap/service list, «Заказать» wherever a Part cannot be bought, the Category picture for a Part without photos, `cacheKey` stability (same data, same key; changed rendered data, new key), `ai-catalog.json`. Prior art: `catalogueSnapshot.test.ts`, `catalogue.test.ts`, `llmsTxt.test.ts`, `paths.test.ts`.
2. Browser elements under jsdom in `packages/site-kit` (100% coverage): "My garage" stores only a resolved VIN (#430).
3. Shop admin and store routes through `medusaIntegrationTestRunner`: the privacy-filtered Order summary behind «Сделать кейс» (no VIN, name or contact), completing and cancelling an Order when the bot asks, the shop marking the Lead lost on a cancel, and the cart and checkout refactors (#388-#390) with today's specs passing unchanged plus unit tests for every refusal code of the pure judge. Prior art: the offer-cart, checkout and carlab-orders specs.
4. Content schemas and copy: the content and i18n tests for the Work schema (sourced Parts, price) and the new service; the em-dash/Ё check with its own test; the YAML validity check. Prior art: `content.test.ts`, `.github/scripts/yaml-content-valid.ts`.
5. Design (#289, #37, #39 placement, header search): no automated tests; a `ui-designer` pass with mobile-first screenshots of the homepage, the header on phone and desktop, a service page, a Part page with «Заказать» and «Установить у нас», and a Parts sourcing Work.
6. The CRM bot's won and lost handlers in `packages/lead-crm` (100% coverage) with a stubbed shop: won completes the Order, lost cancels it, a failed call is retried, a non-Order Lead calls nothing. Prior art: the bot callback and `afterStatusChange` tests.
7. The carlab.rs route that commits the draft Work, against a stubbed GitHub and a stubbed shop summary: one unpublished Work file with car, Parts and RSD total, committed with the caller's Keystatic token, refused without one. Prior art: approved.rs's case-photo routes and `githubContents.ts` tests.

## Out of Scope

- Firing the shop funnel goals (`add_to_cart`, `begin_checkout`, `purchase`) and registering conversions (#384-#387): they ship with opening the shop (#382, #383).
- Opening the shop itself (#382, #383) and its legal blockers (#76, #79).
- On-demand rendering of catalogue pages (#423, deferred).
- WebMCP (#431).
- A full redesign or a new visual direction for carlab.rs (#289 is rescoped to polish).
- Collecting the social account URLs (the owner supplies them).

## Further Notes

- Grilled on 2026-10-30 (decisions recorded in GLOSSARY.md: Parts sourcing, Parts inquiry, Completed order; CONTEXT.md: Case study; ADR-0053).
- Owner decisions on 2026-10-30: #289 is polish of the current style around two touchpoints (service booking and part search) that both end in a contact; parts sourcing becomes a service and Works list sourced parts with two-way links; the funnel stays with opening the shop; #37 follows the design polish's button rule; social accounts exist and links come later.
- #268 needs the owner's Keyword Planner and Search Console access; #380's last step needs the shop's first production deploy.
- The folded tickets should be closed with a pointer to this spec once their part lands.
